transcript.content: Hello, thank you for coming in. Can you tell me what’s been bothering you or what brings you here today?

Hi. Um... well, I guess I'm here because flying has started to feel... a lot scarier than it really should. 

Just the idea of getting on a plane, I... I just picture the turbulence from my honeymoon flight again. I mean, I know people fly safely every day, but... yeah. That's what brings me in.
Can you tell me more about what happened during that turbulence on your honeymoon flight and how it affected you emotionally at the time?
Um... it was just... really bumpy. The plane was shaking a lot. I don't really remember all the exact details, it was just... bad. I guess I was just really scared. That's... pretty much it.
Is it specifically the memory of that turbulence that scares you, or do you feel anxious about flying in general, even when there isn’t turbulence?
Um... I'm not really sure. I guess... just flying in general now. I just don't like getting on planes anymore. I try not to think about it too much.
When you think about flying now, do you worry that you might have a panic attack or feel trapped during the flight?
Um... I don't know. I guess I just... worry about being up there. I haven't really thought about panic attacks or anything like that. I just... I just don't like it.
When you think about flying now, does the fear feel like it’s mainly about experiencing turbulence again, or is it more about flying itself, even when everything seems safe?

Um... I guess it's both. Just... the idea of getting on a plane makes me picture that turbulence again. Even though I know people fly safely every day, it just... it feels way scarier than it should. So... yeah.

Do you avoid flying mainly because you’re worried about having a panic attack or feeling physical symptoms like rapid heartbeat or shortness of breath, or is it more about a general sense of fear related to being on a plane?
Um... I don't really think about panic attacks. I just... I just don't like being on planes. It's just the flying part, I guess.
When you think about flying, do you ever worry that you might experience physical symptoms like a racing heart, sweating, or dizziness, even if there's no turbulence?
Um... I don't think so. I don't really get dizzy or anything like that. I just... I just don't like it.
When you imagine or think about being on a plane, do you ever feel sudden, intense panic or a strong urge to escape, even if there’s no actual danger?

Um... yeah, I guess I do get a little panicked. Just... like if I have to look up flights for work, for a conference or something... or even just hearing a plane outside. My chest just gets tight right away. I just... I get this rush where I feel like I need to close my laptop or just... stop thinking about it. So, yeah.
How long have you felt this way about flying, and do you go out of your way to avoid booking flights even for important events or responsibilities?

Um... it's been a while, I guess. I try not to fly. If there's a work training, I'll usually just drive, even if it takes a long time. Or I just... I won't go. If I absolutely have to book something, or even talk about going somewhere, I... I make my husband sit with me. Just so I don't back out.

When you avoid flying, is it mainly because you’re afraid of having a panic attack or feeling physical symptoms during the flight, or is it more about a general fear of being on the plane itself, even if you don’t have physical symptoms?
Um... I don't really know. I just... I just don't like planes. It's not really about having a panic attack, I don't think. I just... I don't want to be on one.

When you think about flying or are exposed to reminders of flying, do you ever worry that you might lose control, have a panic attack, or be unable to escape or get help if you start feeling very anxious?
Um... no, not really. I don't... I don't really think about losing control or anything. I just... I just don't like the idea of being on a plane. That's all.

When you avoid flying, is it mainly because you’re afraid something bad might happen during the flight, like a crash, or is it more about how you feel physically or emotionally if you start getting anxious?
Um... I'm not really sure. I don't really sit around thinking about a crash or anything like that. I just... I avoid it because I don't want to do it. That's pretty much it.

Have you ever had an unexpected, sudden episode of intense fear or discomfort while on a plane or thinking about flying, where you felt like something terrible was going to happen right away, like you might suffocate, go crazy, or have a heart attack?
No... I haven't ever felt like that. I don't think I'm going to have a heart attack or suffocate or anything extreme like that. I just... I just stay away from planes.
Is your fear of flying mainly about something specific, like turbulence or being high up, or is it more of a general uncomfortable feeling without a clear reason?

Um... I guess it's... specific. Like the turbulence. Flying has just started to feel... way scarier than it really should. I know people fly safely every day, but... just the idea of getting on a plane, I just keep picturing the turbulence from my honeymoon flight. So... yeah. I guess it's that.

Is your fear mostly triggered when you specifically think about turbulence or situations similar to your honeymoon flight, or does it also come up in other flying situations that don’t involve turbulence, like takeoff, landing, or just being at high altitude?
Um... I guess I'm not really sure. I just... I don't really know if it's just the turbulence. I just don't like flying.

When you feel afraid about flying, does the fear only come up when you specifically think about turbulence, or does it also happen even when you're just thinking about flying smoothly without any turbulence?
I don't know... I just don't like thinking about flying at all. It's just... I just try not to think about it.
When you feel afraid about flying, does the fear happen even in situations where you're not thinking about turbulence, like just seeing a plane or hearing about someone else flying?

Um... yeah, I guess so. Like... if I have to look up flights for a work conference, or... or even just hear a plane overhead outside. My chest just... it gets tight right away. I get this rush of panic, and I just... I usually just have to shut my laptop or try to get away from the thought.
When you feel afraid about flying, does the fear mainly come from the idea of experiencing turbulence again, or do you feel fear even when you know the flight will be smooth and safe?
I don't really know... I just... I don't think it matters if it's supposed to be smooth. I just... I don't want to be on a plane.
